title: Book Two · Chapter 31: The Blue Skirt
story:
Mum is wearing the blue skirt when Ronan comes home on Wednesday.

He almost walks past her. Then he stops by the table.

“You cut the long cloth.”

“Yes. I wanted you to see my shoes.”

He looks at the bottom. It ends above her shoes. There is no loose blue cloth across the bed now.

“Can you walk in it?”

Mum takes three large steps towards him. Ronan jumps aside.

“Yes,” she says. “Can you?”

She lifts one side a little. He can see the neat line inside. The pale mark is hidden in the fold.

“Dad said it was very long.”

“It was. Now the long end is in my scrap bag.”

Mum turns towards the window. The blue changes in the light. Ronan puts his school bag down and looks again.

“Did you make the pocket too?”

She puts her hand inside it. “For my keys. And perhaps a coin.”

“Or a very small book.”

“Then I would walk in a circle.”

He laughs. Mum takes the skirt off again. She hangs it inside, away from her work table. A customer's trousers are waiting there.

Ronan sits with his picture book. He reads part of a new page, then looks at the skirt again.

“Are you wearing it somewhere?”

“To see my friend on Sunday.”

“Am I coming?”

“Not this time. You and Dad can make your own plans.”

He does not like that answer at first. Sunday sounds better with a visit in it. Then he thinks of the blue bike. Dad may have time for another ride.

He cannot ask yet. Dad is still at work.

Ronan finds the short bowl story in his bag. He puts it beside the picture book. The two pages are different sizes. His own notes fit along the side of the story copy.

At school today, Jun wanted to borrow a pencil. Ronan gave him the longer one. Jun returned it after lunch, with the point still sharp.

Ronan takes out both pencils now. He sharpens the short one over a scrap of paper. The wood curls down beside his thumb.

Mum comes to check his hand.

“Slowly. And keep the knife away from your leg.”

She stays beside him until he is done. Then she puts the little knife away herself.

Dad comes home near dinner. He sees the skirt on its hook.

“Where is the long end?”

“In Mum's scrap bag,” Ronan tells him.

“Good. I thought I might still be holding it.”

Mum laughs from the kitchen.

Ronan tells Dad about Sunday. Dad does not promise a long trip. He needs to check his work first. A short walk may be possible.

After dinner, Mum tries the skirt once more. Dad holds the light. Ronan looks at the pocket.

“Your keys are in there.”

“I know.”

“You can hear them.”

Mum takes one step. The keys make a small sound. She leaves them there.
